page: Microsoft Azure D160alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 80 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 320.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core.

For local data requirements, the instance includes 9449 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. The processor architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions (such as avx512f, avx512_vnni, and avx512_bf16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data places this server in the top tier (top 10%) across almost all evaluated metrics. It demonstrates exceptional multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 287,625.19 and a PassMark CPU score of 145,894.28. Memory performance is highly efficient, achieving a read-only cached bandwidth of 14,559.08 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 209.95 GB/sec. Database operations are highly performant, with Redis SET operations reaching 202.38 million operations per second. For language model tasks, prompt processing speeds reach 6,083.87 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 366.92 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

Given its high vCPU count relative to memory capacity, the D160alds_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The integration of a large 9449 GB local disk makes it highly suitable for high-throughput database operations, intensive software compilation, ray tracing, and high-volume static web serving.
description: The Microsoft Azure D160alds_v7 is a high-performance, compute-optimized virtual machine utilizing the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers 160 dedicated vCPUs across 80 physical cores at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, paired with 320.0 GB of RAM. This configuration yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, optimized for compute-dense workloads. The server features a substantial 9449 GB local storage disk and supports Premium Storage. Benchmark results place the instance in the top 10% for multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations. It supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and SHA-NI, but lacks GPU acceleration. This server is highly suited for compute-intensive tasks, large-scale database operations, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
